messages:
mike: Quick Q — we got a small ambiguity in the /v1/generate contract. If a client sends `model_id` + `model_hint` + `region_hint`, what's the canonical precedence and what do we guarantee in the response? specifically: is `served_model` guaranteed to exist (string vs object), and any backward-compat notes for older SDKs that might send `model` instead of `model_id`?

sara: Short answer: precedence is `model_id` (hard pin) > `model_hint` (soft preference) > default selection. `region_hint` is routing-only (best-effort). `served_model` was added last quarter and should be present for new endpoints but marked optional for backward compat. Older SDKs that send `model` will be mapped server-side to `model_id` for now, but we should document deprecation. :white_check_mark:

kevin: can you confirm fallback order when `model_id` is pinned but unavailable in region? e.g., do we pick same family quantized variant, or prefer same tier in another region? also want exact param names to use in SDK mapping. quick sample request below — is this what we expect?
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_id": "redwood-7b",
  "model_hint": "redwood-7b-opt",
  "region_hint": "us-west-2",
  "tier_hint": "prod",
  "fallback_policy": "auto"
}
```

mike: yes that's the payload shape from the client side. question: is `fallback_policy` an enum? and what's the canonical string values so SDKs can expose them?

diana: fallback behavior we run today is: 1) exact `model_id` in requested region; 2) compatible variant (quantized / lower-precision) in requested region; 3) same `model_id` in closest region with capacity; 4) model family fallback (e.g., 7b -> 3b) respecting `tier_hint`; 5) if `fallback_policy`==`none` we return 503 instead. So yes, enum values: `auto` (default), `region-only`, `none`. We'll add `prefer-variant` if teams want to prefer quantized variants over cross-region.

kevin: nice. for SDK mapping: map legacy `model` -> `model_id` server-side and emit a deprecation header `X-Old-Model-Usage` to clients for 30 days? should we also return a `served_model` header or inside response body?

sara: prefer body field `served_model` (string) for quick programmatic checks; header `X-Served-Model` for infra/observability is fine too. `served_model` should be a compact identifier like `redwood-7b-quant-v2@gpu:g4dn`. we avoid deep objects to keep contract stable. if we want more detail, include optional `served_model_details` as a freeform JSON string in `X-Served-Model-Info` header (so older clients ignore).

api-lint-bot: automated lint: response-schema-change detected — new optional field `served_model` (string). Recommend: bump minor, add migration notes to SDKs, and add contract test that accepts both presence/absence. See https://internal.redwood.dev/schema/changes/served_model-2150000123

diana: action items: 1) docs PR to update param precedence + fallback_policy enum; 2) router unit test for fallback order; 3) SDK PR to map `model`->`model_id` and surface deprecation header. @kevin can you take SDK + docs? i'll own router test.

kevin: taking SDK + docs. ETA EOD tomorrow for docs, PR for SDK Monday. will add unit tests to ensure clients see `served_model` when present and tolerate missing field. ping @mike for review. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — trivial followups: please include example curl and a note about `region_hint` being best-effort. also add one-liner about privacy: `served_model` may include region tag but not customer PII.

diana: noted. i'll add the privacy note in the router doc. closing out here unless anyone has more edge cases.

kevin: one last: do we want a compatibility smoke test that runs old SDK (uses `model`) against canary? i'll add to SDK pipeline if you want.

sara: yes please, add a nightly compat job that sends `model` and verifies mapping and deprecation header. thanks all.
